title: Razorpay Expands MandateHQ to Power HDFC Bank with a Unified Card Mandate Experience
summary: Razorpay MandateHQ powers HDFC Bank’s unified recurring card mandate platform across portal hubs and merchant apps-making HDFC Bank the first bank in India to offer customers a single view of their recurring card mandates across portals and merchants.
body_markdown:
Every recurring card payment starts with a card your bank issued. What happens after that first payment has never really belonged to the bank.


The customer sets up a Netflix subscription. An Amazon Prime renewal. An insurance premium. A monthly SIP. A gym membership. A cloud software plan. Each one is authorised on the same card, and each one immediately disappears into a different place: a merchant’s settings page, an app store, a separate mandate portal. The bank issued the card, but the relationship went somewhere else.


Today, that changes. Introducing Razorpay MandateHQ Expansion, Now Powering HDFC Bank


Razorpay MandateHQ Expansion brings every card mandate back to where it started: your bank. HDFC Bank is the first bank to go live with a unified mandate portal built on it.


## **The problem: everything exists, nothing connects**


Millions of card mandates are created every month in India. From the customer’s side, they are scattered across hundreds of merchants, dozens of apps and multiple mandate hubs. Each merchant exposes only its own mandate. There is no single destination where a cardholder can see all of them, let alone manage them.


Try the exercise yourself. Count how many subscriptions you have on your card. Now count how many different places you would have to visit to pause or cancel each one.


From the bank’s side, the fragmentation is just as real. Issuers end up running multiple platforms and integrations, delivering inconsistent customer experiences, absorbing higher operational costs, and carrying the burden of keeping every one of those systems aligned with regulation.


And regulation is not optional. RBI’s framework for recurring card payments puts the issuer squarely at the centre of customer control. Banks are required to provide:


- OTP-based mandate authorisation


- 24-hour pre-debit notifications


- Self-service mandate management (view, pause, cancel)


- Post-debit confirmations


- Additional authentication for high-value debits above ₹5,000


- A customer grievance redressal mechanism


RBI has laid out the vision for a unified view of recurring mandates. Until now, the infrastructure to deliver it did not exist in one place.


## **Why now**


Three forces make this the moment.


- **Recurring payments are scaling fast.** Recurring transactions are projected to grow at close to 40% CAGR over the next four years. For banks, that does not just mean more transactions. It means more mandates, more notifications, more compliance obligations and more operational overhead, unless the underlying infrastructure changes.


- **Regulation is pushing control to the issuer.** Every new requirement, from pre-debit alerts to high-value authentication, lands on the bank. Meeting them across a patchwork of systems gets harder every year.


- **Customer expectations have moved.** People manage their money in their banking app. They increasingly expect to manage their recurring payments there too, not in fifteen different merchant settings screens.


The old way won’t scale. The next era needs one platform.


## **What Razorpay’s MandateHQ Expansion does**


MandateHQ is Razorpay’s unified mandate platform built for banks and issuers. It powers the complete card mandate lifecycle, from authorisation through notifications, debit processing and customer controls, and gives the bank a single, bank-owned experience to put in front of every cardholder.


- **A unified view of every card mandate.** Customers see every mandate associated with their cards in one bank-hosted experience, including mandates that were registered through other hubs and platforms. OTT,, insurance, investments, utilities and software subscriptions collapse into a single list.


- **Complete self-service lifecycle management.** From that one list, a customer can open any mandate and view, pause, resume or cancel it, review debit history, see upcoming debits, and complete any required authentication, without ever leaving the bank’s experience.


- **Compliance journeys, built in.** OTP-based authorisation, 24-hour pre-debit notifications across SMS, email and WhatsApp, post-debit confirmations and additional authentication for high-value debits are all handled on the platform, so the bank stays compliant without stitching journeys together across systems.


- **A unified admin and operations layer.** On the bank side, MandateHQ provides a single dashboard for mandate, debit and customer-action reporting, configurable roles and permissions, analytics, notification status and operational visibility across the whole recurring portfolio.


- **An open platform.** MandateHQ can surface mandates registered with other hubs rather than restricting the customer’s view to mandates originated inside MandateHQ. That is what makes “every card mandate” possible, and what removes the operational complexity of running parallel systems.


- **Plug in, go live.** Banks do not need to build recurring-payment infrastructure from scratch. MandateHQ is API-based and integrates into existing payments infrastructure, dramatically reducing go-live time.


## **HDFC Bank: the first unified mandate portal**


HDFC Bank is the first bank to offer its cardholders a unified portal for card mandate management, powered by Razorpay MandateHQ.


For an HDFC Bank cardholder, the experience is simple. Log in. See every card mandate in one list, across merchants, apps and platforms. Tap into one. Pause it, resume it, cancel it, or approve a high-value debit. Everything happens inside HDFC Bank’s own interface.


Behind that experience, HDFC Bank gets a single platform managing authorisation, notifications, debit processing and customer actions, with a unified operations dashboard on top.


This is the transformation we built MandateHQ Expansion around: the moment when fifteen disconnected mandate experiences become one.


## **What it means for banks**


MandateHQ Expansion moves the bank from simply issuing the payment instrument to owning the recurring-payment experience. The outcomes follow from that shift:


- **A better customer experience.** One trusted place to see and control every card mandate.


- **Lower operational complexity.** One platform instead of many integrations, with unified reporting and controls.


- **Stronger recurring-payment control.** Complete lifecycle management, with compliance journeys built in rather than bolted on.


- **Enterprise-grade reliability and performance.** MandateHQ is architected for 99.99% availability, and banks can see up to 5% higher success rates on recurring transactions.


- **Fewer chargebacks and disputes.** When customers can see and manage every mandate, surprise debits and the grievances that follow them go down.


## **One place. Every card mandates.**


At Razorpay, we have spent years building for the Indian subscription economy, first for businesses, then for their customers. MandateHQ Expansion completes the picture: an end-to-end recurring payments stack that now includes the bank, the place where every recurring payment starts and where customer trust already lives.


Recurring payments should not live across dozens of experiences. They should live where trust already exists. Your bank.
